subject.title: gh-issues skill: untrusted issue body injected directly into sub-agent prompt

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this issue by requiring a runtime untrusted-content boundary for gh-issues plus per-spawn child tool scoping, or accept prompt-level guidance/global subagent policy as sufficient hardening?
rationale: The source-reproducible gap is real, but the permanent API/security boundary affects spawned-agent tool policy, persisted session state, prompt construction, and what SECURITY.md treats as vulnerability versus hardening.

options.title: Require runtime boundary and toolsAllow
options.body: Land or replace the open toolsAllow work and add gh-issues content wrapping/summarization or equivalent runtime isolation before considering this issue fixed.

options.title: Accept prompt-only mitigation
options.body: Treat a narrowed prompt-policy update as sufficient defense-in-depth while documenting that hostile issue bodies remain within the operator-granted agent trust boundary.

options.title: Defer pending broader design
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers design a unified delegated-agent content and capability policy across skills, hooks, and sessions_spawn.

recommendation.title: Require runtime boundary and toolsAllow
recommendation.body: Land or replace the open toolsAllow work and add gh-issues content wrapping/summarization or equivalent runtime isolation before considering this issue fixed.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current history across sessions_spawn, sandbox inheritance, docs, and this issue's surrounding maintainer review context.
